user_questions.question: Which source should the unified profile use for app accounts, and which keys should decide that two records are the same customer? Options: (a) CRM Contact records via the Salesforce CRM connector, with Contact.Pronto_App_Account_Id__c (198 of 198 populated) as the app account ID, together with Loyalty_Transaction__c and Review__c (recommended); (b) an external Pronto app system through the Ingestion API. Keys: app account ID only, or app account ID plus email (one email is shared by 2 Contacts).
user_questions.simulated_answer: Ingest Contact, Loyalty Transaction, Review via CRM connector; identity resolution on Pronto App Account Id + email; calculated insight for lifetime points.

skill_friction: Split-retry accounting is ambiguous: 'A split sends both halves and counts as one retry' does not say what happens when one half times out and the other succeeds. I resent only the failed half, narrower, as the second retry; the rule could be read as requiring both halves again.

Data Cloud metadata type names (DataStreamDefinition, MktDataTranObject, ObjectSourceTargetMap, IdentityResolution, MktCalcInsightObjectDef) and their Module paths cannot be verified with the allowed commands, and neither SKILL.md nor spec-format.md gives canonical types or folders for Data Cloud rows; I used 'Not specified' for Module and recorded the types as assumptions.

The spec-format rule to put every data stream, DLO, DMO, and mapping on its own row inflates a Data Cloud spec to 15 Setup-delivered rows; guidance on whether Setup-generated DLOs are separate deployable rows would help.

Rule 'Every component the spec names, including rejected candidates, is verified to exist' conflicts with naming platform-generated Data Cloud objects (standard ssot__ DMOs, unified link objects) that do not exist until provisioning; the org-verification note covers ssot__Individual__dlm but not how to name them in the spec.

The step 5 'predict the answer' rule and the business-value 'ask' rule both applied to the 'lifetime points' definition (Earn-only vs net); I decided (Earn-only, sign-independent) rather than spend the second message, but the skill does not say which rule wins when a safe default exists for a business definition.
An answer to a scope question added scope (the calculated insight); the skill says added scope becomes part of the requirement but gives no guidance on whether D1/D2 must be re-run for the new scope.

Runner deviation: D2 was not sent. D1 did not cover automation, so the skill required it; behavior on the three objects (triggers, flows, Apex readers, connector permission sets) was covered by org queries instead (seq 9, 11, 12), and Section 2 does not state that D2 was skipped. The workflow could make the D2-skip condition an explicit checkpoint.
